newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals has spelled out the measures which would have to be in place for the country to contemplate a "big bang" lifting of exchange controls.
- Competition policy is to be addressed with renewed vigour by government, which named two new Competition Board members on Tuesday.
- Edgars Stores reported a five percent drop in attributable earnings to 145.1 million rand in the six months to September, after consumers cut back on credit spending and Jet plunged into the red.
- Gencor won shareholder approval for the merger of its four Evander gold mines after a last-minute deal with dissident shareholder Mercury Asset Management.
- Producer price inflation ticked up to 7.6 percent in September from August's 7.4 percent, surprising economists who had expected a sharp rise as a result of higher oil prices and the weak rand.
- Shell may prove a world class gas deposit in Namibia when it completes final tests next week on a well drilled off the country's south coast.
- State-owned Transnet has uncovered 121 cases of company credit card abuse by its employees.
- Post and telecommunications minister Jay Naidoo has run into a full-scale private-sector rebellion over his management of the modernisation of South Africa's telephone sector.
- Alec Erwin, the trade and industry minister, has appointed two outspoken critics of conglomerates and monopolies to the Competition Board.
- Vuna Industrial, the industrial arm of Thebe Investments, has bought a 34 percent stake in property services group JHI Holdings in a cash-and-equity swap estimated at 15 million rand.
- Edgars Stores reported a seven percent drop in earnings per share to 271 cents for the six months to September 30.
- Hundreds of panic-stricken residents queued for tests at the Oudtshoorn hospital on Tuesday, after an outbreak of the deadly Congo Fever among the town's ostrich abattoir workers.
